paragraphs.text: Καὶ μετὰ τὰ ἀρώματα ταῦτα κατὰ βορρᾶν ἐθεώρησα τὰ ὄρη ἑπτὰ πεπληρωμένα νάρδου καθαρᾶς καὶ εὐώδων δένδρων καὶ κιννάμωμον καὶ πιπέρεως.
paragraphs.translit: Kai meta ta arōmata tauta kata borran etheōrēsa ta orē hepta peplērōmena nardou katharas kai euōdōn dendrōn kai kinnamōmon kai pipereōs.

i18n.en: And after these aromatic places, toward the north I beheld the seven mountains, filled with pure nard and fragrant trees and cinnamon and pepper.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἐπορεύθην ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκρωτηρίας πάντων τῶν ὀρέων τούτων κατὰ ἀνατολὴν τῆς γῆς πορρωτέρω, καὶ διῆλθον ἐπὶ τὴν ἐρυθρὰν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐπεξήλθων αὐτῇ πορρωτέρω, καὶ διῆλθον ἐπὶ τὸν Ζωτιήλ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ekeithen eporeuthēn epi tas akrōtērias pantōn tōn oreōn toutōn kata anatolēn tēs gēs porrōterō, kai diēlthon epi tēn erythran thalassan kai epexēlthōn autē porrōterō, kai diēlthon epi ton Zōtiēl.

i18n.en: And from there I journeyed to the summits of all these mountains, far toward the east of the earth, and I passed over the Erythraean Sea, and went on far beyond it, and I passed over by Zotiel.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἦλθον πρὸς παράδεισον τῆς δικαιοσύνης· καὶ ἐθεώρουν ἐπέκεινα τῶν δένδρων τούτων δένδρα πολλὰ καὶ μεγάλα φυόμενα ἐκεῖ, ἔνδοξα καὶ μεγάλα καὶ καλά, καὶ ἔνδοξον τὸ δένδρον τῆς σοφίας, ἐξ ἧς ἐσθίουσιν καὶ γινώσκουσιν σοφίαν μεγάλην.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēlthon pros paradeison tēs dikaiosynēs; kai etheōroun epekeina tōn dendrōn toutōn dendra polla kai megala phyomena ekei, endoxa kai megala kai kala, kai endoxon to dendron tēs sophias, ex hēs esthiousin kai ginōskousin sophian megalēn.

i18n.en: And I came to the Garden of Righteousness; and beyond those trees I beheld many great trees growing there — glorious and great and beautiful — and the glorious tree of wisdom, from which they eat and come to know great wisdom.

paragraphs.commentary: **The tree of wisdom** — Raphael identifies as the Gen 3 tree of which Adam and Eve ate. The 1 En 32 'tree of wisdom' redeploys the Hebrew Bible *etz ha-da'at tov va-ra* 'tree of the knowing of good and bad' with the Second-Temple-Jewish *Sophia* / *Hokhmah* personification-vocabulary. The 1 En 32 framing is more nuanced than the Hebrew Bible reading: 'they learned wisdom and their eyes were opened' is quasi-positive. See central entry `tree-of-wisdom-1-enoch-32-gen-3-sophia-cross-corpus`. Cross-corpus to Prov 8 + Wis Sol 7-9 (the Sophia-personification tradition); to Gnostic-Christian readings (Hypostasis of the Archons; Apocryphon of John); to existing central entries `etz-chayim-daat`, `niphqecho-eineihem`, `ke-elohim`.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὅμοιον ἦν τὸ δένδρον ἐκεῖνο τῇ κερατέᾳ, καὶ ὁ καρπὸς αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ βότρυς ἀμπέλου πάγκαλος, καὶ ἡ ὀσμὴ τοῦ δένδρου διέτρεχεν πόρρωθεν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai homoion ēn to dendron ekeino tē kerateā, kai ho karpos autou hōsei botrys ampelou pankalos, kai hē osmē tou dendrou dietrechen porrōthen.

i18n.en: And that tree was like the carob, and its fruit was like the cluster of the vine, exceedingly beautiful; and the fragrance of the tree ran out from afar.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ εἶπον· Ὡς καλὸν τὸ δένδρον τοῦτο, καὶ ὡς εὐῶδες καὶ ὡραῖον ἐν τῇ ὄψει.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eipon; Hōs kalon to dendron touto, kai hōs euōdes kai hōraion en tē opsei.

i18n.en: And I said: How beautiful is this tree, and how fragrant, and lovely to look upon!

paragraphs.text: ወአውሥአኒ፡ ሩፋኤል፡ ቅዱስ፡ መልአክ፡ ዘምስሌየ፡ ሀሎ፡ ወይቤ፡ ዝውእቱ፡ ዕፀ፡ ጥበብ፡ ዘበልዑ፡ እምኔሁ፡ አቡከ፡ ዘትካት፡ ወእምከ፡ ዘትካት፡ ቅድሜከ፡ ወአእመሩ፡ ጥበበ፡ ወተከሥቱ፡ አዕይንቲሆሙ፡ ወአእመሩ፡ ከመ፡ ዕራቆሙ፡ እሙንቱ፡ ወተሰዱ፡ እምነ፡ ገነት፡
paragraphs.translit: wa-ʾawśaʾanī Rufāʾēl qəddus malʾak za-məslēya hallo wa-yəbē; zə-wəʾətu ʿəḍa ṭəbab za-balʿu ʾəmənnehu ʾabuka za-təkat wa-ʾəmməka za-təkat qədmēka wa-ʾaʾmaru ṭəbaba wa-takasətu ʾaʿyəntihomu wa-ʾaʾmaru kama ʿərāqomu ʾəmuntu wa-tasaddu ʾəmənna gannat

i18n.en: And Raphael, the holy angel who was with me, answered and said: This is the tree of wisdom, from which your ancient father and your ancient mother — those who came before you — ate, and learned wisdom, and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they were driven out of the garden.

paragraphs.commentary: Raphael's identification 'this is the tree of wisdom of which thy father old and thy aged mother ate' — the textual fountainhead of the Second-Temple-Jewish Sophia / Hokhmah tradition's reading of the Gen 3 tree-of-knowledge as the tree-of-wisdom.
